## P2 - `apply` cannot add a `mgmt-net` link on a management network that does not exist yet; verification fails with a cryptic `bridge ""` error

**Location:** [core/apply.go:130-148](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/apply.go#L130-L148)

**Problem:** When a management network referenced by a `mgmt-net` link does not exist, `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` &#40;[`core/network.go:207-220`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/network.go#L207-L220)&#41; deliberately leaves the link node&#39;s shortname empty, and both `bridgeMasterMismatch` &#40;[`core/topology_reconcile.go:928-943`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/topology_reconcile.go#L928-L943)&#41; and `TestResolveMgmtNetLinkNetworksAutoBridge` treat the unresolved bridge as an expected, tolerated state. However, the `apply` path runs `checkApplyTopologyDefinition` &#40;[`core/apply.go:146`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/apply.go#L146-L146)&#41;, which invokes `Link.Verify` with `RunBridgeExistsCheck: true`, before `prepareApply` &#40;[`core/apply.go:198`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/apply.go#L198-L198)&#41; creates the missing networks. `CheckBridgeExists` &#40;[`links/endpoint_bridge.go:62-71`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/links/endpoint_bridge.go#L62-L71)&#41; then calls `netlink.LinkByName("")` and returns `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`.

**Trigger:** A user edits a deployed topology to add a new `mgmt` list entry plus a `mgmt-net` link with `network: <new-network>` &#40;bridge driver, no explicit bridge&#41;, then runs `clab apply` or a reconcile `clab deploy` on the existing lab. On Podman the path is the same&#58; `resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` swallows the `mgmtRuntime` error at [`core/network.go:188-193`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/network.go#L188-L193) with `log.Debug`, so the clear &#34;runtime does not support multiple management networks&#34; message never surfaces and the empty-bridge error appears instead.

**Impact:** The primary incremental scenario of the feature fails before `apply` can create the network. Fresh deploy works only because deploy creates networks before topology verification &#40;`prepareLabManagementNetwork`, [`core/deploy.go:306-321`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/deploy.go#L306-L321), which re-runs `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` after `CreateNetwork`&#41;. The user-facing error gives no actionable guidance.

**Suggested correction:** Tolerate an unresolved bridge in verification the same way `bridgeMasterMismatch` does&#58; skip the bridge-existence check in `EndpointBridge.Verify`/`CheckBridgeExists` for a nodeless `mgmt-net` endpoint with an empty shortname. With that tolerance the existing flow completes&#58; `prepareApply` creates the network, sets `m.Bridge`, re-runs `setMgmtNetLinkBridges`, and `deployLinks` deploys against the real bridge. If instead `apply` is meant to only attach to existing networks, surface a clear error in `setMgmtNetLinkBridges`/`resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` &#40;including the currently swallowed `mgmtRuntime` error&#41; instead of letting the empty shortname reach verification.


## P4 - Magic string `"mgmt-net"` duplicated in `bridgeMasterMismatch` instead of reusing `mgmtNetOwnerName`

**Location:** [core/topology&#95;reconcile.go:928-943](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/topology_reconcile.go#L928-L943)

**Problem:** The new `bridgeMasterMismatch` helper hardcodes `bridge == "mgmt-net"` for the nodeless skip condition, while the `links` package centralizes the same logical owner name as `mgmtNetOwnerName` &#40;[`links/link_mgmt-net.go:115-119`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/links/link_mgmt-net.go#L115-L119)&#41;. The constant is unexported, so `core` cannot reference it today.

**Trigger:** Any future change to the logical owner name or the special node name would silently break the reconciler&#39;s skip condition while the `links` package keeps working.

**Impact:** Low maintenance cost only; both spellings denote the same logical name by this PR&#39;s design.

**Suggested correction:** Optional&#58; export the constant from the `links` package and use it in `bridgeMasterMismatch`, or move the skip predicate into the `links` package so `core` does not need to know the marker scheme.


## P4 - `defaultMgmtNetworkName = "clab"` duplicates `dockerNetName`

**Location:** [labruntime/clabernetes/files.go:45-47](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/labruntime/clabernetes/files.go#L45-L47)

**Problem:** The new clabernetes constant `defaultMgmtNetworkName = "clab"` restates the default management network name that [`core/config.go:33`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/config.go#L33-L33) already owns as `dockerNetName`.

**Trigger:** Any change to the default network name in `core` leaves the clabernetes fallback out of sync, producing brief `links` whose default-network matching diverges between the two packages.

**Impact:** Low; both values are `"clab"` today and the duplication is confined to one fallback expression.

**Suggested correction:** Optional&#58; export the constant from `core` and use it in `labruntime/clabernetes`, or let the clabernetes default flow through the same code path that resolves `config.Mgmt` defaults.


## Coverage

- Source-only review of head revision 1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c; no tests were executed and no code was run.
- Traced fresh-deploy ordering &#40;networks created and bridges set before topology verification, so fresh deploy is unaffected by the P2 finding&#41;, the `apply` ordering &#40;source of the P2 finding&#41;, `planApply` endpoint discovery for the logical `mgmt-net` node across networks, ownership marker creation and legacy compatibility, destroy flows &#40;`WithSkippedMgmtNetLinksCheck`, `resolveExistingMgmtNetworks`, `GetMgmtBrLinkNodes` special-node deletion&#41;, clabernetes brief-link rejection, and the schema addition for the `mgmt-net` network key.
- The Podman limitation &#40;no `MgmtNetBinder`/`ForMgmtNet`&#41; is intentional and documented in [`docs/rn/0.80.md:72`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/docs/rn/0.80.md#L72-L72); Podman still implements `MgmtBridgeResolver` for default-network `mgmt-net` `links`. The cryptic apply-time error Podman users see is covered by the P2 finding.
- The package-level &#95;mgmtBrLinkNodes map is shared across labs in one process &#40;a pre-existing pattern, previously a single node&#41;; keys are network names, which bounds cross-lab interaction to same-named networks. No defect found; noted for awareness.
- Removals of `SetMgmtNetUnderlyingBridge` from [`core/exec.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/exec.go#L1-L1) and [`core/save.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/save.go#L1-L1) are safe&#58; those flows neither resolve nor deploy `mgmt-net` `links`, and tools veth uses plain bridge endpoints.
- Docs updates in [`docs/manual/network.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/docs/manual/network.md#L1-L1) and [`docs/manual/topo-def-file.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md#L1-L1) accurately describe the new network key, the default-network fallback, and the bridge-driver requirement.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

540: +func (c *CLab) mgmtNetLinkNetworks() []*clabtypes.MgmtNet {
541: +	if c.Config.Topology == nil {

548: +		}

560: +// resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks populates the bridge names of the non-default management
561: +// networks that mgmt-net links reference without an explicit bridge. The runtime names
562: +// such a bridge when it creates the network, so the bridge of an existing network is
563: +// looked up from the runtime. The lookup neither creates networks nor changes host
564: +// state, so it is safe for dry runs. Networks that do not exist yet are left unresolved.
565: +func (c *CLab) resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks(ctx context.Context) error {
566: +	var resolved clabtypes.MgmtNetworks
567: +	for _, m := range c.mgmtNetLinkNetworks() {
568: +		if m == c.Config.Mgmt || m.Bridge != "" || slices.Contains(resolved, m) {
569: +			continue
570: +		}
571: +		resolved = append(resolved, m)
572: +
573: +		rt, err := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
574: +		if err != nil {
575: +			// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks
576: +			log.Debug("Skipping management network resolution", "network", m.Network, "error", err)
577: +			continue
578: +		}
579: +		resolver, ok := rt.(clabruntime.MgmtBridgeResolver)
580: +		if !ok {
581: +			continue
582: +		}
583: +		if err := resolver.ResolveMgmtBridge(ctx); err != nil {
584: +			return err
585: +		}
586: +	}
587: +	return nil
588: +}

590: +// setMgmtNetLinkBridges points the mgmt-net link nodes of the management networks
591: +// that mgmt-net links select at the bridge of that network.
592: +func (c *CLab) setMgmtNetLinkBridges() error {
593: +	if err := clablinks.SetMgmtNetUnderlyingBridge(c.Config.Mgmt.Bridge); err != nil {
594: +		return err
595: +	}
596: +	for _, m := range c.mgmtNetLinkNetworks() {
597: +		if m == c.Config.Mgmt || m.Network == "" {
598: +			continue
599: +		}
600: +		if err := clablinks.SetMgmtNetworkUnderlyingBridge(m.Network, m.Bridge); err != nil {
601: +			return err
602: +		}
603: +	}
604: +	return nil
605: +}

890: +func TestResolveMgmtNetLinkNetworksAutoBridge(t *testing.T) {
891: +	registerMgmtResolveRuntime()
892: +
893: +	for _, tc := range []struct {
894: +		name          string
895: +		networkExists bool
896: +		wantBridge    string
897: +	}{
898: +		{name: "existing network is resolved", networkExists: true, wantBridge: "br-fake"},
899: +		{name: "missing network is not created", networkExists: false, wantBridge: ""},
900: +	} {
901: +		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
902: +			// a CreateNet call would change host state, e.g. during a dry run
903: +			setMgmtResolveBehavior(t, &mgmtResolveBehavior{
904: +				checkable:     true,
905: +				networkExists: tc.networkExists,
906: +				failCreateNet: true,
907: +			})
908: +
909: +			c, err := NewContainerLab(
910: +				WithTimeout(time.Minute),
911: +				WithTopoPath(writeTopo(t, mgmtNetLinkAutoBridgeTopo), nil),
912: +				WithRuntime("mgmtresolvetest", &clabruntime.RuntimeConfig{}),
913: +				WithSkippedBindsPathsCheck(),
914: +			)
915: +			if err != nil {
916: +				t.Fatal(err)
917: +			}
918: +
919: +			if err := c.resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks(context.Background()); err != nil {
920: +				t.Fatal(err)
921: +			}
922: +			if err := c.setMgmtNetLinkBridges(); err != nil {
923: +				t.Fatal(err)
924: +			}
925: +			// the mgmt-net link nodes are shared by the package, release their endpoints
926: +			t.Cleanup(c.resetResolvedLinks)
927: +			if err := c.ResolveLinks(); err != nil {
928: +				t.Fatal(err)
929: +			}
930: +
931: +			stats := mgmtResolveRuntimeStatsPtr.Load()
932: +			if got := stats.resolveCalls.Load(); got != 1 {
933: +				t.Fatalf("ResolveMgmtBridge calls = %d, want 1", got)
934: +			}
935: +			if got := stats.createNetCalls.Load(); got != 0 {
936: +				t.Fatalf("CreateNet calls = %d, want 0", got)
937: +			}
938: +
939: +			var got string
940: +			for _, ep := range c.Endpoints {
941: +				if ep.GetIfaceName() == "r1-eth1" {
942: +					got = ep.GetNode().GetShortName()
943: +				}
944: +			}
945: +			if got != tc.wantBridge {
946: +				t.Fatalf("mgmt-net link attached to %q; want %q", got, tc.wantBridge)
947: +			}
948: +		})
949: +	}
950: +}

1072:  ### Drivers
1073:  
1074:  The driver specifies the type of network that is created. Either `bridge` or `macvlan`. 
1075: @@ -727,10 +728,37 @@ topology:
1076:  
1077:  In the above example the node `n1` connects with its `e1-1` interface to the management network. This is done by specifying the endpoint with a reserved name `mgmt-net` and defining the name of the interface that should be used in that bridge (`n1-e1-1`).
1078:  
1079:  By specifying `mgmt-net` name of the node in the endpoint definition we tell containerlab to find out which bridge is used by the management network of our lab and use this bridge as the attachment point for our veth pair.
1080:  
1081: +With [multiple management networks](#multiple-management-networks) the brief form attaches to the first network in the `mgmt` list. To attach to a different network, use the [extended `mgmt-net` link](topo-def-file.md#mgmt-net) definition and set the `network` key to the name of the management network:
1082: +
1083: +```yaml
1084: +name: multi
1085: +mgmt:
1086: +  - network: oob
1087: +    ipv4-subnet: 172.31.10.0/24
1088: +  - network: lab
1089: +    ipv4-subnet: 172.31.20.0/24
1090: +    bridge: br-lab
1091: +topology:

1094: +      kind: linux
1095: +      image: alpine
1096: +      mgmt-net: oob

1099: +      network: lab
1100: +      endpoint:
1101: +        node: r1
1102: +        interface: eth1
1103: +      host-interface: r1-eth1
1104: +```
1105: +

1128:

17: func (c *CLab) CreateNetwork(ctx context.Context) error {
18: 	defined := c.allMgmtNetworks()
19: 	networks := make(clabtypes.MgmtNetworks, 0, len(defined))
20: 	for _, m := range defined {
21: 		if c.skipMgmtNetwork(m) {
22: 			log.Debug("Skipping management network, no node uses it", "network", m.Network)
23: 			continue
24: 		}
25: 		networks = append(networks, m)
26: 	}
27: 	return c.createNetworks(ctx, networks)
28: }
29: 
30: // createNetworks creates or inspects the given management networks
31: // and labels the nodes with their management bridge.
32: func (c *CLab) createNetworks(ctx context.Context, networks clabtypes.MgmtNetworks) error {
33: 	for _, m := range networks {
34: 		var opts []clabruntime.NetworkCreateOptions
35: 		if addresses := c.staticManagementAddresses(m); len(addresses) != 0 {
36: 			opts = append(opts, clabruntime.NetworkCreateOptions{StaticAddresses: addresses})
37: 		}
38: 
39: 		rt, err := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
40: 		if err != nil {
41: 			return err
42: 		}
43: 		// create docker network or use existing one
44: 		if err := rt.CreateNet(ctx, opts...); err != nil {
45: 			return err
46: 		}
47: 
48: 		// VM kinds read the subnets at init, before the runtime resolved them
49: 		for _, cfg := range c.mgmtNetNodes(m) {
50: 			for key, subnet := range map[string]string{
51: 				"DOCKER_NET_V4_ADDR": m.IPv4Subnet,
52: 				"DOCKER_NET_V6_ADDR": m.IPv6Subnet,
53: 			} {
54: 				if value, ok := cfg.Env[key]; ok && value == "" {
55: 					cfg.Env[key] = subnet
56: 				}
57: 			}
58: 		}
59: 	}
60: 
61: 	// save mgmt bridge name as a label
62: 	for _, n := range c.Nodes {
63: 		bridge := c.globalRuntime().Mgmt().Bridge
64: 		if m := c.mgmtNetByNetwork(n.Config().MgmtNet); m != c.Config.Mgmt {
65: 			bridge = m.Bridge
66: 		}
67: 		n.Config().Labels[clabconstants.NodeMgmtNetBr] = bridge
68: 	}
69: 
70: 	return nil
71: }

73: // mgmtNetNodes returns the configs of the nodes attached to the given management network.
74: func (c *CLab) mgmtNetNodes(m *clabtypes.MgmtNet) []*clabtypes.NodeConfig {
75: 	var configs []*clabtypes.NodeConfig
76: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
77: 		if c.mgmtNetByNetwork(node.Config().MgmtNet) == m {
78: 			configs = append(configs, node.Config())
79: 		}
80: 	}
81: 	return configs
82: }
83: 
84: // SyncMgmtHostRoutes reconciles host routes to current macvlan management endpoints.
85: func (c *CLab) SyncMgmtHostRoutes(ctx context.Context) error {
86: 	if c.Config == nil || c.Config.Mgmt == nil {
87: 		return nil
88: 	}
89: 	c.mgmtRouteMu.Lock()
90: 	defer c.mgmtRouteMu.Unlock()
91: 	for _, m := range c.allMgmtNetworks() {
92: 		if m.Driver != clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan || !m.MacvlanAuxEnabled() {
93: 			continue
94: 		}
95: 		rt, err := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
96: 		if err != nil {
97: 			return err
98: 		}
99: 		if err := rt.SyncMgmtHostRoutes(ctx); err != nil {
100: 			return err
101: 		}
102: 	}
103: 	return nil
104: }
105: 
106: func (c *CLab) staticManagementAddresses(m *clabtypes.MgmtNet) []netip.Addr {
107: 	var addresses []netip.Addr
108: 	for _, config := range c.mgmtNetNodes(m) {
109: 		if address, err := netip.ParseAddr(config.MgmtIPv4Address); err == nil {
110: 			addresses = append(addresses, address)
111: 		}
112: 		if address, err := netip.ParseAddr(config.MgmtIPv6Address); err == nil {
113: 			addresses = append(addresses, address)
114: 		}
115: 	}
116: 	return addresses
117: }

119: // validateManagementLinks checks that every mgmt-net link references a defined
120: // management network that is backed by a bridge.
121: func (c *CLab) validateManagementLinks() error {
122: 	if c.Config.Topology == nil {
123: 		return nil
124: 	}
125: 	for _, link := range c.Config.Topology.Links {
126: 		if link == nil || link.Link == nil {
127: 			continue
128: 		}
129: 		mgmtNetLink, ok := link.Link.(*clablinks.LinkMgmtNetRaw)
130: 		if !ok {
131: 			continue
132: 		}
133: 		m, err := c.mgmtNetByName(mgmtNetLink.Network)
134: 		if err != nil {
135: 			return fmt.Errorf("mgmt-net link: %w", err)
136: 		}
137: 		if m.Driver == clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {
138: 			if mgmtNetLink.Network == "" {
139: 				return fmt.Errorf(
140: 					"mgmt-net links require a bridge management network and cannot be used with mgmt.driver %q",
141: 					m.Driver,
142: 				)
143: 			}
144: 			return fmt.Errorf(
145: 				"mgmt-net links require a bridge management network and cannot use management network %q with driver %q",
146: 				m.Network,
147: 				m.Driver,
148: 			)
149: 		}
150: 	}
151: 	return nil
152: }
153: 
154: // mgmtNetLinkNetworks returns the management networks referenced by mgmt-net links.
155: func (c *CLab) mgmtNetLinkNetworks() []*clabtypes.MgmtNet {
156: 	if c.Config.Topology == nil {
157: 		return nil
158: 	}
159: 	var networks []*clabtypes.MgmtNet
160: 	for _, link := range c.Config.Topology.Links {
161: 		if link == nil || link.Link == nil {
162: 			continue
163: 		}
164: 		mgmtNetLink, ok := link.Link.(*clablinks.LinkMgmtNetRaw)
165: 		if !ok {
166: 			continue
167: 		}
168: 		if m, err := c.mgmtNetByName(mgmtNetLink.Network); err == nil {
169: 			networks = append(networks, m)
170: 		}
171: 	}
172: 	return networks
173: }
174: 
175: // resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks populates the bridge names of the non-default management
176: // networks that mgmt-net links reference without an explicit bridge. The runtime names
177: // such a bridge when it creates the network, so the bridge of an existing network is
178: // looked up from the runtime. The lookup neither creates networks nor changes host
179: // state, so it is safe for dry runs. Networks that do not exist yet are left unresolved.
180: func (c *CLab) resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks(ctx context.Context) error {
181: 	var resolved clabtypes.MgmtNetworks
182: 	for _, m := range c.mgmtNetLinkNetworks() {
183: 		if m == c.Config.Mgmt || m.Bridge != "" || slices.Contains(resolved, m) {
184: 			continue
185: 		}
186: 		resolved = append(resolved, m)
187: 
188: 		rt, err := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
189: 		if err != nil {
190: 			// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks
191: 			log.Debug("Skipping management network resolution", "network", m.Network, "error", err)
192: 			continue
193: 		}
194: 		resolver, ok := rt.(clabruntime.MgmtBridgeResolver)
195: 		if !ok {
196: 			continue
197: 		}
198: 		if err := resolver.ResolveMgmtBridge(ctx); err != nil {
199: 			return err
200: 		}
201: 	}
202: 	return nil
203: }
204: 
205: // setMgmtNetLinkBridges points the mgmt-net link nodes of the management networks
206: // that mgmt-net links select at the bridge of that network.
207: func (c *CLab) setMgmtNetLinkBridges() error {
208: 	if err := clablinks.SetMgmtNetUnderlyingBridge(c.Config.Mgmt.Bridge); err != nil {
209: 		return err
210: 	}
211: 	for _, m := range c.mgmtNetLinkNetworks() {
212: 		if m == c.Config.Mgmt || m.Network == "" {
213: 			continue
214: 		}
215: 		if err := clablinks.SetMgmtNetworkUnderlyingBridge(m.Network, m.Bridge); err != nil {
216: 			return err
217: 		}
218: 	}
219: 	return nil
220: }

222: // AllocateToolManagementIPs assigns addresses when the topology uses containerlab IPAM.
223: func (c *CLab) AllocateToolManagementIPs(ctx context.Context, cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig) error {
224: 	m := c.mgmtNetByNetwork(cfg.MgmtNet)
225: 	if m.IPAM.Provider == clabtypes.IPAMProviderRuntime {
226: 		return nil
227: 	}
228: 	// tools attach to a network on demand, so it is created even when it is
229: 	// flagged as skipped-when-unused by the topology
230: 	if err := c.createNetworks(ctx, clabtypes.MgmtNetworks{m}); err != nil {
231: 		return err
232: 	}
233: 	reserved, err := c.collectReservedManagementAddresses(ctx, m, nil)
234: 	if err != nil {
235: 		return err
236: 	}
237: 	return mgmt.AllocateManagementIPs(
238: 		ctx,
239: 		m,
240: 		[]*clabtypes.NodeConfig{cfg},
241: 		clabtypes.AllocationOptions{Reserved: reserved},
242: 	)
243: }
244: 
245: // skipMgmtNetwork reports whether the management network m must not be created
246: // because it is not used: skip-when-unused is set on it and no node attached to
247: // it resolves to a network mode that attaches to the management network.
248: func (c *CLab) skipMgmtNetwork(m *clabtypes.MgmtNet) bool {
249: 	if m == nil || !m.SkipWhenUnused {
250: 		return false
251: 	}
252: 
253: 	topo := c.Config.Topology
254: 	if topo == nil || len(topo.Nodes) == 0 {
255: 		return false
256: 	}
257: 
258: 	// a network that mgmt-net links attach to is in use
259: 	if slices.Contains(c.mgmtNetLinkNetworks(), m) {
260: 		return false
261: 	}

47: 	result.RecreatedNodes = sortedStringSet(plan.recreatedNodeSet)
48: 	result.StartedNodes = sortedStringSet(plan.startNodeSet)
49: 	result.AddedLinks = applyLinkNames(plan.addedLinks)
50: 	result.DeletedEndpoints = applyDeletedEndpointNames(plan.staleEndpoints)
51: 	result.RestartedNodes = sortedStringSet(unionStringSets(
52: 		plan.restartNodeSet,
53: 		plan.linkRestartNodeSet,
54: 	))
55: 
56: 	for nodeName, reason := range plan.nodeChangeReasons {
57: 		result.NodeChangeReasons[nodeName] = reason
58: 	}
59: 
60: 	return result
61: }

63: // Apply deploys a lab if it is absent, otherwise it aligns the deployed lab with the
64: // desired topology using runtime state as baseline.
65: func (c *CLab) Apply(
66: 	ctx context.Context,
67: 	options *ApplyOptions,
68: ) (*ApplyResult, error) {
69: 	if options == nil {
70: 		var err error
71: 		options, err = NewApplyOptions(0)
72: 		if err != nil {
73: 			return nil, err
74: 		}
75: 	}
76: 
77: 	if c.Config.Name == "" {
78: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("missing lab name")
79: 	}
80: 	if !c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileIsSet() {
81: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
82: 			"apply requires a topology file; provide --topo when it cannot be derived from --name",
83: 		)
84: 	}
85: 
86: 	currentNodes, err := c.runtimeNodeGroups(ctx)
87: 	if err != nil {
88: 		return nil, err
89: 	}
90: 
91: 	return c.apply(ctx, options, currentNodes)
92: }
93: 
94: func (c *CLab) apply(
95: 	ctx context.Context,
96: 	options *ApplyOptions,
97: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
98: ) (*ApplyResult, error) {
99: 	initialDeploy, err := c.needsInitialDeploy(currentNodes)
100: 	if err != nil {
101: 		return nil, err
102: 	}
103: 	if initialDeploy {
104: 		result := &ApplyResult{
105: 			DryRun:      options.dryRun,
106: 			DeployedLab: true,
107: 			LabName:     c.Config.Name,
108: 		}
109: 
110: 		if options.dryRun {
111: 			return result, nil
112: 		}
113: 
114: 		deployOptions, err := NewDeployOptions(options.maxWorkers)
115: 		if err != nil {
116: 			return nil, err
117: 		}
118: 		deployOptions.SetSkipPostDeploy(options.skipPostDeploy).
119: 			SetSkipLabDirFileACLs(options.skipLabDirFileACLs).
120: 			SetGraph(options.graph).
121: 			SetExportTemplate(options.exportTemplate)
122: 
123: 		if _, err := c.deploy(ctx, deployOptions); err != nil {
124: 			return nil, err
125: 		}
126: 
127: 		return result, nil
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	if err := c.setMgmtBridgeFromRuntime(currentNodes); err != nil {
131: 		return nil, err
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	if err := c.resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks(ctx); err != nil {
135: 		return nil, err
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	if err := c.setMgmtNetLinkBridges(); err != nil {
139: 		return nil, err
140: 	}
141: 
142: 	if err := c.ResolveLinks(); err != nil {
143: 		return nil, err
144: 	}
145: 
146: 	if err := c.checkApplyTopologyDefinition(ctx); err != nil {
147: 		return nil, err
148: 	}
149: 
150: 	plan, err := c.planApply(ctx, currentNodes)
151: 	if err != nil {
152: 		return nil, err
153: 	}
154: 
155: 	if options.dryRun {
156: 		result := applyResultFromPlan(plan)
157: 		result.DryRun = true
158: 		return result, nil
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	if err := c.reconcileNodes(ctx, plan); err != nil {
162: 		return nil, err
163: 	}
164: 
165: 	if plan.empty() {
166: 		if c.tailscaleProxyEnabled() {
167: 			if err := c.updateRuntimeInfoForExistingNodes(ctx); err != nil {
168: 				return nil, err
169: 			}
170: 		}
171: 		if err := c.syncTailscaleProxy(ctx); err != nil {
172: 			return nil, err
173: 		}
174: 		if options.finalizeNoop {
175: 			if err := c.prepareApply(
176: 				ctx,
177: 				nil,
178: 				options.skipLabDirFileACLs,
179: 				currentNodes,
180: 			); err != nil {
181: 				return nil, err
182: 			}
183: 		}
184: 		if err := c.SyncMgmtHostRoutes(ctx); err != nil {
185: 			return nil, err
186: 		}
187: 		if options.finalizeNoop {
188: 			if _, err := c.finalize(ctx, options.exportTemplate, options.graph); err != nil {
189: 				return nil, err
190: 			}
191: 		} else {
192: 			c.writeState()
193: 		}
194: 		return applyResultFromPlan(plan), nil
195: 	}
196: 
197: 	deployNodeNames := plan.deployNodeNames()
198: 	if err := c.prepareApply(
199: 		ctx,
200: 		deployNodeNames,
201: 		options.skipLabDirFileACLs,
202: 		currentNodes,
203: 	); err != nil {
204: 		return nil, err
205: 	}
206: 
207: 	if err := c.deleteApplyEndpoints(ctx, plan.staleEndpoints); err != nil {
208: 		return nil, err
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	if err := c.parkRecreatedNodes(ctx, plan); err != nil {
212: 		return nil, err
213: 	}
214: 
215: 	if err := c.deleteApplyNodes(ctx, plan); err != nil {
216: 		return nil, err
217: 	}
218: 
219: 	if err := c.deployApplyNodes(ctx, plan, options.maxWorkers); err != nil {
220: 		return nil, err
221: 	}
222: 
223: 	if err := c.restoreRecreatedNodes(ctx, plan); err != nil {
224: 		return nil, err
225: 	}
226: 
227: 	if err := c.removeApplyLinkEndpoints(ctx, plan.addedLinks); err != nil {
228: 		return nil, err
229: 	}
230: 
231: 	if err := c.deployLinks(ctx, plan.addedLinks, deployNodeNames); err != nil {
232: 		return nil, err
233: 	}
234: 
235: 	if err := c.postDeployApplyNodes(ctx, deployNodeNames, options.skipPostDeploy); err != nil {
236: 		return nil, err
237: 	}
238: 
239: 	if err := c.restartApplyNodes(ctx, plan.linkRestartNodeSet); err != nil {
240: 		return nil, err
241: 	}
242: 
243: 	if err := c.updateRuntimeInfoForExistingNodes(ctx); err != nil {
244: 		return nil, err
245: 	}
246: 	if err := c.syncTailscaleProxy(ctx); err != nil {
247: 		return nil, err
248: 	}
249: 	if err := c.SyncMgmtHostRoutes(ctx); err != nil {
250: 		return nil, err
251: 	}
252: 
253: 	if _, err := c.finalize(ctx, options.exportTemplate, options.graph); err != nil {
254: 		return nil, err
255: 	}
256: 
257: 	return applyResultFromPlan(plan), nil
258: }
259: 
260: func (c *CLab) checkApplyTopologyDefinition(ctx context.Context) error {
261: 	params := *clablinks.NewVerifyLinkParams()
262: 	if len(c.Endpoints) > 0 {
263: 		runtime := c.globalRuntime()
264: 		if runtime == nil {
265: 			return fmt.Errorf("container runtime is not initialized")
266: 		}
267: 		config := runtime.Config()
268: 		if config.VerifyLinkParams != nil {
269: 			params = *config.VerifyLinkParams
270: 		}
271: 	}
272: 	params.AllowExistingEndpoint = true
273: 	if err := c.verifyLinks(ctx, &params); err != nil {
274: 		return err
275: 	}
276: 
277: 	if err := c.verifyRootNetNSLinks(); err != nil {
278: 		return err
279: 	}
280: 
281: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
282: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].CheckDeploymentConditions(ctx); err != nil {
283: 			return err
284: 		}
285: 	}
286: 
287: 	if err := c.verifyDuplicateAddresses(); err != nil {
288: 		return err
289: 	}
290: 
291: 	return c.verifyTailscaleProxy()
292: }
293: 
294: func (c *CLab) prepareApply(
295: 	ctx context.Context,
296: 	addedNodes []string,
297: 	skipLabDirFileACLs bool,
298: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
299: ) error {
300: 	existing := c.collectExistingManagementAddresses(currentNodes)
301: 	if err := c.prepareLabManagementNetwork(ctx, existing...); err != nil {
302: 		return err
303: 	}
304: 
305: 	if err := c.prepareDeployArtifacts(ctx, skipLabDirFileACLs); err != nil {
306: 		return err
307: 	}
308: 
309: 	for _, nodeName := range addedNodes {
310: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].PullImage(ctx); err != nil {
311: 			return err
312: 		}
313: 	}
314: 
315: 	return nil
316: }
317: 
318: func (*CLab) removeApplyLinkEndpoints(ctx context.Context, links []clablinks.Link) error {
319: 	for _, link := range links {
320: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
321: 			if err := clablinks.RemoveOwnedInterface(
322: 				ctx,
323: 				ep.GetNode(),
324: 				ep.GetIfaceName(),
325: 			); err != nil {
326: 				return err
327: 			}
328: 		}
329: 	}
330: 
331: 	return nil
332: }
333: 
334: // try to preserve the existing addressing instead of reallocation.
335: func (c *CLab) collectExistingManagementAddresses(
336: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
337: ) []clabtypes.ExistingAddress {
338: 	var existing []clabtypes.ExistingAddress
339: 	for name, group := range currentNodes {
340: 		for _, ctr := range group.containers {
341: 			if c.mgmtNetByNetwork(ctr.NetworkName).Network != ctr.NetworkName {
342: 				continue
343: 			}
344: 			for _, value := range []string{ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv4addr, ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv6addr} {
345: 				if ip, err := netip.ParseAddr(value); err == nil {
346: 					existing = append(
347: 						existing,
348: 						clabtypes.ExistingAddress{NodeName: name, ContainerID: ctr.ID, Address: ip},
349: 					)
350: 				}
351: 			}
352: 		}
353: 	}
354: 	return existing
355: }

383: 
384: 	// extra networks without subnets get them from the runtime's address pools,
385: 	// node addresses within them are still assigned by the IPAM provider
386: 	if isDefault && m.Driver != clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {
387: 		if m.IPv4Subnet == "" && m.IPv6Subnet == "" {

868: // GetLinkNodes returns all CLab.Nodes nodes as links.Nodes enriched with the special nodes -
869: // host and mgmt-net. The CLab nodes are copied to a new map and thus clab.Node interface is
870: // converted to link.Node.
871: func (c *CLab) getLinkNodes() map[string]clablinks.Node {
872: 	// resolveNodes is a map of all nodes in the topology
873: 	// that is artificially created to combat circular dependencies.
874: 	// If no circ deps were in place we could've used c.Nodes map instead.
875: 	// The map is used to resolve links between the nodes by passing it in the ResolveParams struct.
876: 	resolveNodes := make(map[string]clablinks.Node, len(c.Nodes))
877: 	for k, v := range c.Nodes {
878: 		resolveNodes[k] = v
879: 	}
880: 
881: 	// add the virtual host and mgmt-bridge nodes to the resolve nodes
882: 	specialNodes := c.getSpecialLinkNodes()
883: 	for _, n := range specialNodes {
884: 		resolveNodes[n.GetShortName()] = n
885: 	}
886: 
887: 	return resolveNodes
888: }
889: 
890: // GetSpecialLinkNodes returns a map of special nodes that are used to resolve links.
891: // Special nodes are host and mgmt-bridge nodes that are not typically present in the topology file
892: // but are required to resolve links.
893: func (*CLab) getSpecialLinkNodes() map[string]clablinks.Node {
894: 	// add the virtual host and mgmt-bridge nodes to the resolve nodes
895: 	specialNodes := map[string]clablinks.Node{
896: 		"host":     clablinks.GetHostLinkNode(),
897: 		"mgmt-net": clablinks.GetMgmtBrLinkNode(),
898: 	}
899: 
900: 	return specialNodes
901: }
902: 
903: // ResolveLinks resolves raw links to the actual link types and stores them in the CLab.Links map.
904: func (c *CLab) ResolveLinks() error {
905: 	c.resetResolvedLinks()
906: 
907: 	resolveParams := &clablinks.ResolveParams{
908: 		Nodes:              c.getLinkNodes(),
909: 		DefaultMgmtNetwork: c.Config.Mgmt.Network,
910: 		NodesFilter:        c.nodeFilter,
911: 		LabName:            c.Config.Name,
912: 	}
913: 
914: 	for i, l := range c.Config.Topology.Links {
915: 		l, err := l.Link.Resolve(resolveParams)
916: 		if err != nil {
917: 			return err
918: 		}
919: 
920: 		// if the link is nil, it means that it was filtered out
921: 		if l == nil {
922: 			continue
923: 		}
924: 
925: 		c.Endpoints = append(c.Endpoints, l.GetEndpoints()...)
926: 		c.Links[i] = l
927: 	}
928: 
929: 	return nil
930: }
931: 
932: func (c *CLab) resetResolvedLinks() {
933: 	for _, ep := range c.Endpoints {
934: 		if ep == nil || ep.GetNode() == nil {
935: 			continue
936: 		}
937: 		_ = ep.GetNode().ReleaseEndpoint(ep)
938: 	}
939: 
940: 	c.Endpoints = nil
941: 	c.Links = make(map[int]clablinks.Link)
942: }

944: // extractDNSServers extracts DNS servers from the resolv.conf files
945: // and populates the Nodes DNS Config with these if not specifically provided.
946: func (c *CLab) extractDNSServers(filesys fs.FS) error {
947: 	// extract DNS servers from the relevant resolv.conf files
948: 	DNSServers, err := clabutils.ExtractDNSServersFromResolvConf(filesys,
949: 		[]string{"etc/resolv.conf", "run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf"})
950: 	if err != nil {
951: 		return err
952: 	}
953: 
954: 	// no DNS Servers found, return
955: 	if len(DNSServers) == 0 {
956: 		return nil
957: 	}
958: 
959: 	// if no dns servers are explicitly configured,
960: 	// we set the DNS servers that we've extracted.
961: 	for _, n := range c.Nodes {
962: 		config := n.Config()
963: 		// skip nodes in container network mode since docker doesn't allow
964: 		// setting dns config for them
965: 		if strings.HasPrefix(config.NetworkMode, "container") {
966: 			log.Debugf(
967: 				"Skipping DNS config for node %s as it is in container network mode",
968: 				config.ShortName,
969: 			)
970: 
971: 			continue
972: 		}
973: 
974: 		if config.DNS == nil {
975: 			config.DNS = &clabtypes.DNSConfig{}
976: 		}
977: 
978: 		if n.Config().DNS.Servers == nil {
979: 			n.Config().DNS.Servers = DNSServers
980: 		}
981: 	}
982: 
983: 	return nil
984: }

Reasoning
Important finding candidate: `getSpecialLinkNodes()` still only includes the **default** mgmt-net node (`GetMgmtBrLinkNode()`), keyed as `"mgmt-net"`. But `getLinkNodes()` puts special nodes into `resolveNodes` keyed by `n.GetShortName()`. All `mgmtBridgeLinkNode` instances now share shortname `"mgmt-net"`, so even if all were added, the map would collapse them. But since Resolve uses `getMgmtBrLinkNode(network)` directly (not via the Nodes map), the resolution of mgmt-net links does not go through the map. The map's `mgmt-net` entry is used for what? Probably for endpoint lookup elsewhere or `verifyRootNetNSLinks`. Hmm.

But wait — a real problem: `getSpecialLinkNodes()["mgmt-net"]` returns only the default node, whose shortname is set to the default bridge by setMgmtNetLinkBridges. In `topology_reconcile.go` line 649: `node, exists := c.getSpecialLinkNodes()[nodeName]` — what's this used for? Let me check. If an apply plan needs to look up special nodes for endpoints of non-default mgmt-net links, the endpoint's node is the per-network mgmtBridgeLinkNode, but getSpecialLinkNodes only has the default. Let me check that code.

Also `deploy.go` line 247: `eps := c.getSpecialLinkNodes()["host"].GetEndpoints()` — host only.

Let me look at topology_reconcile.go around 649 and the apply plan endpoints handling.

371: func (c *CLab) collectReservedManagementAddresses(
372: 	ctx context.Context,
373: 	m *clabtypes.MgmtNet,
374: 	existing []clabtypes.ExistingAddress,
375: ) ([]netip.Addr, error) {
376: 	var subnets []netip.Prefix
377: 	for _, value := range []string{m.IPv4Subnet, m.IPv6Subnet} {
378: 		if value == "" {
379: 			continue
380: 		}
381: 		subnet, err := netip.ParsePrefix(value)
382: 		if err != nil {
383: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("management subnet %q: %w", value, err)
384: 		}
385: 		subnets = append(subnets, subnet)
386: 	}
387: 	occupied, err := c.globalRuntime().NetworkAddresses(ctx, subnets)
388: 	if err != nil {
389: 		return nil, err
390: 	}
391: 	type ownerAddress struct {
392: 		containerID string
393: 		address     netip.Addr
394: 	}
395: 	reused := make(map[ownerAddress]bool, len(existing))
396: 	for _, entry := range existing {
397: 		if entry.ContainerID != "" {
398: 			reused[ownerAddress{entry.ContainerID, entry.Address}] = true
399: 		}
400: 	}
401: 
402: 	var reserved []netip.Addr
403: 	for _, entry := range occupied {
404: 		if entry.NetworkName == m.Network &&
405: 			reused[ownerAddress{entry.ContainerID, entry.Address}] {
406: 			continue
407: 		}
408: 		reserved = append(reserved, entry.Address)
409: 	}
410: 	return reserved, nil
411: }

Good — `bridgeNameFromInspect` is a pre-existing helper reused in `ResolveMgmtBridge`. Reuse is good.

Now check deploy flow: fresh deploy: `ResolveLinks()` is called BEFORE `prepareLabManagementNetwork`! Line 190: `err = c.ResolveLinks()` then line 206 `c.prepareLabManagementNetwork(ctx)` (which creates networks then calls `setMgmtNetLinkBridges`). So during fresh deploy: ResolveLinks resolves mgmt-net links with the mgmt nodes whose shortnames are still stale/"" — but resolution just creates endpoint objects; the bridge shortname is read later at deploy time (`AddLinkToContainer` uses `b.shortname` → `netlink.LinkByName`). So order is fine: setMgmtNetLinkBridges after CreateNetwork sets the bridge names before endpoints are deployed (createNodes comes after prepareLabManagementNetwork at line 224). Good.

But wait: `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` iterates `mgmtNetLinkNetworks()` — for networks where `m.Bridge == ""` (e.g., network exists check failed / skipMgmtNetwork skipped a network?) — hmm. Consider: a mgmt-net link selects network X with skip-when-unused: true, and no nodes attach to X (only the mgmt-net link). skipMgmtNetwork now keeps X because mgmtNetLinkNetworks contains X. Good — covered by the test.

Now consider: network X used by mgmt-net link, X's driver is bridge but `m.Bridge` is "" after CreateNet? Does docker CreateNet set m.Bridge? Let me check CreateNet around line 372-420.

Reasoning
So `RunBridgeExistsCheck: true` by default. In apply's `checkApplyTopologyDefinition`, params.RunBridgeExistsCheck stays true (only AllowExistingEndpoint set to true). So `verifyLinks` → EndpointBridge.Verify → CheckBridgeExists(ctx, node) where node is the mgmtBridgeLinkNode with shortname = bridge name.

Scenario: existing lab, user adds a mgmt-net link selecting a **new** non-default management network (defined in mgmt but not yet created). Flow in apply:
1. `resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks`: the network doesn't exist → Bridge stays "".
2. `setMgmtNetLinkBridges`: node shortname = "" for that network.
3. `ResolveLinks`.
4. `checkApplyTopologyDefinition` → `verifyLinks` → for the new mgmt-net endpoint: CheckBridgeExists → `netlink.LinkByName("")` → LinkNotFoundError → error: `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`.

So applying a topology that adds a mgmt-net link to a not-yet-created non-default network fails with a cryptic error, and the network is never created (CreateNetwork runs later in prepareApply). Wait — but actually is this scenario realistic? A user adding `mgmt: - network: lab` and `links: - type: mgmt-net, network: lab` to an existing lab, then running `clab deploy` (reconcile path) or `clab apply`. Deploy reconcile path → apply. Yes, reachable.

Hold on — is the network really not created? CreateNetwork is in prepareLabManagementNetwork called in prepareApply — after the verification failure. So apply aborts. The user sees `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`. Confusing, but it's an error, not silent misbehavior. However — hmm, wait. Was this scenario reachable in base? In base, mgmt-net links could only attach to the default network, whose bridge exists (deployed lab). So this is a new failure mode introduced by the PR. Severity: P2 or P3? It blocks a legitimate operation (adding a mgmt-net link on a new network via apply) with a cryptic error. Actually wait — let me double-check: would the mgmt network be created on a fresh `deploy` after? The lab is already deployed; `clab deploy` reconciles → apply → fails. Only `--reconfigure` or destroy+deploy works. Hmm.

But wait, actually let me double check verifyLinks flow for mgmt-net endpoints: does verifyLinks skip nodeless endpoints? Let me look at verifyLinks implementation and how it filters endpoints.

Reasoning
Confirmed: in apply's `checkApplyTopologyDefinition` (core/apply.go:273), `verifyLinks` runs with `RunBridgeExistsCheck: true`, and the new mgmt-net endpoint for an unresolved network has `GetShortName() == ""` → `CheckBridgeExists` → `netlink.LinkByName("")` → LinkNotFoundError → `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`.

But wait — is there a guard for the empty bridge? In EndpointBridge.Verify: `if (p == nil || p.RunBridgeExistsCheck) && e.Node.GetLinkEndpointType() != LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS` — mgmtBridgeLinkNode type is LinkEndpointTypeBridge, not BridgeNS. So yes, CheckBridgeExists runs.

Hmm, but wait — in the fresh-deploy path, `checkTopologyDefinition` runs AFTER prepareLabManagementNetwork, so bridges are set. In apply path, the check runs BEFORE prepareApply (which creates networks). So adding a mgmt-net link to a new non-default network via apply fails before network creation.

But hold on — is that really the case in base for the default network? In base (and in head for the default network), apply on existing lab: c.Config.Mgmt.Bridge is resolved from runtime by setMgmtBridgeFromRuntime. So the default network always resolves. For a new *non-default* network, there's no bridge until created. So yes, this is a new failure mode.

Also what about the fresh-deploy path via apply? initialDeploy → c.deploy(...) → deploy() → ResolveLinks() → prepareLabManagementNetwork (creates networks, sets bridges) → checkTopologyDefinition. Fine.

What about podman? Podman's MgmtBridgeResolver: does PodmanRuntime support ForMgmtNet (MgmtNetBinder)? Check podman.go for ForMgmtNet. If podman doesn't implement MgmtNetBinder, mgmtRuntime returns error for non-default network → resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks logs debug and skips → mgmt-net link to non-default network with podman resolves to shortname ""... wait no. setMgmtNetLinkBridges would call SetMgmtNetworkUnderlyingBridge(m.Network, m.Bridge) where m.Bridge = "" → shortname "". Then fresh deploy: CreateNetwork → createNetworks → mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m) errors → CreateNetwork fails with "runtime X does not support multiple management networks". OK so podman fails cleanly on fresh deploy. Let me check which runtimes implement MgmtNetBinder.

178: // looked up from the runtime. The lookup neither creates networks nor changes host
179: // state, so it is safe for dry runs. Networks that do not exist yet are left unresolved.
180: func (c *CLab) resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks(ctx context.Context) error {
181: 	var resolved clabtypes.MgmtNetworks
182: 	for _, m := range c.mgmtNetLinkNetworks() {
183: 		if m == c.Config.Mgmt || m.Bridge != "" || slices.Contains(resolved, m) {
184: 			continue
185: 		}
186: 		resolved = append(resolved, m)
187: 
188: 		rt, err := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
189: 		if err != nil {
190: 			// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks
191: 			log.Debug("Skipping management network resolution", "network", m.Network, "error", err)
192: 			continue
193: 		}
194: 		resolver, ok := rt.(clabruntime.MgmtBridgeResolver)
195: 		if !ok {
196: 			continue
197: 		}
198: 		if err := resolver.ResolveMgmtBridge(ctx); err != nil {
199: 			return err
200: 		}
201: 	}
202: 	return nil
203: }
204: 
205: // setMgmtNetLinkBridges points the mgmt-net link nodes of the management networks
206: // that mgmt-net links select at the bridge of that network.
207: func (c *CLab) setMgmtNetLinkBridges() error {
208: 	if err := clablinks.SetMgmtNetUnderlyingBridge(c.Config.Mgmt.Bridge); err != nil {
209: 		return err
210: 	}
211: 	for _, m := range c.mgmtNetLinkNetworks() {
212: 		if m == c.Config.Mgmt || m.Network == "" {
213: 			continue
214: 		}
215: 		if err := clablinks.SetMgmtNetworkUnderlyingBridge(m.Network, m.Bridge); err != nil {
216: 			return err
217: 		}
218: 	}
219: 	return nil
220: }
221: 
222: // AllocateToolManagementIPs assigns addresses when the topology uses containerlab IPAM.
223: func (c *CLab) AllocateToolManagementIPs(ctx context.Context, cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig) error {
224: 	m := c.mgmtNetByNetwork(cfg.MgmtNet)
225: 	if m.IPAM.Provider == clabtypes.IPAMProviderRuntime {
226: 		return nil
227: 	}
228: 	// tools attach to a network on demand, so it is created even when it is
229: 	// flagged as skipped-when-unused by the topology
230: 	if err := c.createNetworks(ctx, clabtypes.MgmtNetworks{m}); err != nil {
231: 		return err
232: 	}
233: 	reserved, err := c.collectReservedManagementAddresses(ctx, m, nil)
234: 	if err != nil {
235: 		return err
236: 	}
237: 	return mgmt.AllocateManagementIPs(
238: 		ctx,
239: 		m,
240: 		[]*clabtypes.NodeConfig{cfg},
241: 		clabtypes.AllocationOptions{Reserved: reserved},
242: 	)
243: }
244: 
245: // skipMgmtNetwork reports whether the management network m must not be created
246: // because it is not used: skip-when-unused is set on it and no node attached to
247: // it resolves to a network mode that attaches to the management network.
248: func (c *CLab) skipMgmtNetwork(m *clabtypes.MgmtNet) bool {
249: 	if m == nil || !m.SkipWhenUnused {
250: 		return false
251: 	}
252: 
253: 	topo := c.Config.Topology
254: 	if topo == nil || len(topo.Nodes) == 0 {
255: 		return false
256: 	}
257: 
258: 	// a network that mgmt-net links attach to is in use
259: 	if slices.Contains(c.mgmtNetLinkNetworks(), m) {
260: 		return false
261: 	}
262: 
263: 	for name := range topo.Nodes {
264: 		if topo.GetNodeNetworkMode(name) == "none" {
265: 			continue
266: 		}
267: 		if c.mgmtNetByNetwork(topo.GetNodeMgmtNet(name)) == m {
268: 			return false
269: 		}
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	return true
273: }
274: 
275: // mgmtNetworksSkipped reports whether every defined management network is
276: // skipped because it is unused.
277: func (c *CLab) mgmtNetworksSkipped() bool {
278: 	for _, m := range c.allMgmtNetworks() {
279: 		if !c.skipMgmtNetwork(m) {
280: 			return false
281: 		}
282: 	}
283: 	return true
284: }

Reasoning
Key observations:

1. `getMgmtBrLinkNode` creates nodes with `shortname: mgmtNetOwnerName` = "mgmt-net" and `AddLinkToContainer` uses `netlink.LinkByName(b.shortname)`. For a non-default network whose bridge is never set (e.g., apply path where network doesn't exist), shortname stays "" → `LinkByName("")` errors at deploy. But since networks get created before deployLinks, this is mostly fine. However — there's a subtle failure mode: **duplicate "mgmt-net" shortname across all mgmt networks**. `GetMgmtBrLinkNodes()` returns nodes all with shortname "mgmt-net" until bridges are set. `verifyRootNetNSLinks` (config.go:582) adds `clablinks.GetMgmtBrLinkNodes()` — all nodes have iface names "mgmt-br" style? Their endpoints have HostInterface names — uniqueness of interface names matters. All nodes share the endpoint iface names? Each mgmt network's node has its own endpoints (added in Resolve: `bridgeEp.GetNode().AddEndpoint(bridgeEp)`). Two mgmt-net links on different networks could use the same HostInterface name (e.g., both use "mgmt-br")? Then verifyRootNetNSLinks would catch duplicate iface names → error. Previously with one network, iface was unique. Now user could define two mgmt-net links with same host iface on different networks — rootNS verify flags duplicate. Actually that IS a real collision: the host-interface names must be unique across all mgmt networks since they all live in rootNS. verifyRootNetNSLinks catches it. Good.

2. **F2: verifyRootNetNSLinks only checks iface name uniqueness, but `CheckBridgeExists`... ** wait, no, verifyRootNetNSLinks doesn't run CheckBridgeExists. OK.

3. `SetMgmtNetworkUnderlyingBridge(network, bridge)`: no validation of empty bridge; sets shortname = "". Then `AddLinkToContainer` → `LinkByName("")` fails. When could a link deploy with empty shortname? 564: 	}

566:

573: 		}
574: 		if runtimeNode.external || runtimeNode.rootNamespaceBased {
575: 			continue
576: 		}
577: 		if len(runtimeNode.containers) > 0 &&
578: 			runtimeNode.containers[0].Labels[clabconstants.NodeKind] == clabnodestailscale.KindName {
579: 			tailscaleContainers = append(tailscaleContainers, runtimeNode.containers...)
580: 			continue
581: 		}
582: 		if node, ok := c.Nodes[nodeName]; ok {
583: 			hookNodes = append(hookNodes, node)
584: 		}
585: 	}
586: 	var logoutWg sync.WaitGroup
587: 	for _, ctr := range tailscaleContainers {
588: 		logoutWg.Go(func() { c.logoutTailscaleContainer(ctx, ctr) })
589: 	}

If state.MgmtNetworks includes default "clab" and defined includes it → skipped. OK.

But subtle issue: `mgmtNetworksForCleanup` merges state-recorded networks. Then in destroy loop, for each m: `m.Network == "bridge"` skip; else `mgmtRuntime` + `rt.DeleteNet(ctx)`. For docker: `ForMgmtNet(m)` — fresh MgmtNet copy; DeleteNet uses r.mgmt.Network. Fine.

3. Hmm — wait, `addMgmtNetworksFromContainers`: this adds networks from containers (destroy-by-name path?). `c.mgmtNetByNetwork(name).Network == name` → continue (already defined). Else append with Bridge from label. OK.

139: func (c *CLab) makeCopyForDestroy(
140: 	ctx context.Context,
141: 	topo,
142: 	labDir string,
143: 	opts DestroyOptions,
144: ) (*CLab, error) {
145: 	newOpts := []ClabOption{
146: 		WithTimeout(c.timeout),
147: 		// a topology edited after deploy may no longer pass the mgmt-net link checks,
148: 		// which must not prevent the removal of the deployed lab.
149: 		WithSkippedMgmtNetLinksCheck(),
150: 	}
151: 
152: 	// Try to load topology file if it exists, otherwise use lab name only.
153: 	// This allows destroying labs even when the topology file has been deleted.
154: 	// WithTopoPath / WithLabNameOnly must run before WithNodeFilter so filterClabNodes
155: 	// sees topology nodes (see filterClabNodes in clab.go).
156: 	varsFiles := opts.varsFiles
157: 	if len(varsFiles) == 0 {
158: 		varsFiles = c.TopoPaths.VarsFilenamesAbsPath()
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	if clabutils.FileOrDirExists(topo) {
162: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithTopoPath(topo, varsFiles))
163: 	} else {
164: 		// Derive lab name from lab directory (format: clab-<labname>)
165: 		labName := filepath.Base(labDir)
166: 		labName = strings.TrimPrefix(labName, "clab-")
167: 		log.Debugf("topology file %q not found, using lab name %q for destroy", topo, labName)
168: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithLabNameOnly(labName))
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	newOpts = append(newOpts,
172: 		WithNodeFilter(opts.nodeFilter),
173: 		// during destroy we don't want to check bind paths
174: 		// as it is irrelevant for this command.
175: 		WithSkippedBindsPathsCheck(),
176: 		WithRuntime(
177: 			c.globalRuntimeName,
178: 			&clabruntime.RuntimeConfig{
179: 				Debug:            c.Config.Debug,
180: 				Timeout:          c.timeout,
181: 				GracefulShutdown: opts.graceful,
182: 			},
183: 		),
184: 	)
185: 
186: 	if opts.keepMgmtNet {
187: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithKeepMgmtNet())
188: 	}
189: 
190: 	cc, err := NewContainerLab(newOpts...)
191: 	if err != nil {
192: 		return nil, err
193: 	}
194: 	if labDir != "" && clabutils.FileOrDirExists(labDir) {
195: 		// adjust the labdir. Usually we take the PWD. but now on destroy time,
196: 		// we might be in a different Dir.
197: 		err = cc.TopoPaths.SetLabDir(labDir)
198: 		if err != nil {
199: 			return nil, err
200: 		}

233: // resolveExistingMgmtNetworks inspects the management networks that already exist
234: // so their bridge names are populated, e.g. for the iptables cleanup on destroy.
235: // Networks that do not exist are skipped: they hold no bridge yet, and the callers
236: // must not create management networks. Runtimes that cannot check network existence
237: // keep the create-or-inspect behavior.
238: func (c *CLab) resolveExistingMgmtNetworks(
239: 	ctx context.Context,
240: 	networks clabtypes.MgmtNetworks,
241: ) error {
242: 	var existing clabtypes.MgmtNetworks
243: 
244: 	for _, m := range networks {
245: 		rt, rtErr := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
246: 		if rtErr != nil {
247: 			// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks
248: 			log.Debug(
249: 				"Skipping management network resolution", "network", m.Network, "error", rtErr,
250: 			)
251: 			continue
252: 		}
253: 
254: 		checker, ok := rt.(clabruntime.MgmtNetworkChecker)
255: 		if !ok {
256: 			existing = append(existing, m)
257: 			continue
258: 		}
259: 
260: 		exists, err := checker.MgmtNetworkExists(ctx)
261: 		if err != nil {
262: 			return err
263: 		}
264: 		if !exists {
265: 			log.Debug("Skipping management network that does not exist", "network", m.Network)
266: 			continue
267: 		}
268: 
269: 		existing = append(existing, m)
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	return c.createNetworks(ctx, existing)
273: }

385: func (c *CLab) destroy(ctx context.Context, maxWorkers uint, keepMgmtNet bool) error {
386: 	var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
387: 	var orphanSidecars []clabruntime.GenericContainer
388: 	var err error
389: 
390: 	// If we have nodes defined (from topology file), list containers by node.
391: 	// Otherwise, list containers by lab name label (for destroy-by-name-only case).
392: 	if len(c.Nodes) > 0 {
393: 		containers, err = c.ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(ctx)
394: 	} else if c.Config.Name != "" {
395: 		containers, err = c.ListContainers(ctx, WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))
396: 	}
397: 
398: 	if err != nil {
399: 		return err
400: 	}
401: 
402: 	if len(c.Nodes) == 0 {
403: 		c.addMgmtNetworksFromContainers(containers)
404: 	}
405: 
406: 	if len(c.Nodes) > 0 {
407: 		tailscaleContainers, err := c.discoverTailscaleContainers(ctx, c.nodeFilter)
408: 		if err != nil {
409: 			return err
410: 		}
411: 		for _, ctr := range tailscaleContainers {
412: 			if _, desired := c.Nodes[ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]]; desired {
413: 				continue
414: 			}
415: 			containers = append(containers, ctr)
416: 			if ctr.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] == "" {
417: 				orphanSidecars = append(orphanSidecars, ctr)
418: 			}
419: 		}
420: 	}
421: 
422: 	if len(containers) == 0 {
423: 		return nil
424: 	}
425: 
426: 	if maxWorkers == 0 {
427: 		maxWorkers = uint(len(containers))
428: 	}

626: // preDestroyNodes runs the PreDestroy stage of the given nodes concurrently, before any of them
627: // is deleted. Nodes without a container are skipped. A workers value of 0 runs all hooks at once.
628: func (*CLab) preDestroyNodes(ctx context.Context, nodes []clabnodes.Node, workers uint) {
629: 	if workers == 0 || workers > uint(len(nodes)) {
630: 		workers = uint(len(nodes))
631: 	}
632: 
633: 	sem := make(chan struct{}, workers)
634: 	wg := new(sync.WaitGroup)
635: 
636: 	for _, n := range nodes {
637: 		wg.Add(1)
638: 		sem <- struct{}{}
639: 
640: 		go func() {
641: 			defer wg.Done()
642: 			defer func() { <-sem }()
643: 
644: 			if n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.NotFound {
645: 				return
646: 			}
647: 
648: 			if err := n.PreDestroy(ctx); err != nil {
649: 				log.Warnf("node %q pre-destroy hook failed: %v", n.Config().ShortName, err)
650: 			}
651: 		}()
652: 	}
653: 
654: 	wg.Wait()
655: }
656: 
657: func (c *CLab) deleteNodes(ctx context.Context, workers uint) {
658: 	wg := new(sync.WaitGroup)
659: 
660: 	concurrentChan := make(chan clabnodes.Node)
661: 
662: 	workerFunc := func(i uint, input chan clabnodes.Node, wg *sync.WaitGroup) {
663: 		defer wg.Done()
664: 
665: 		for {
666: 			select {
667: 			case n := <-input:
668: 				if n == nil {
669: 					log.Debugf("Worker %d terminating...", i)
670: 					return
671: 				}
672: 
673: 				err := n.Delete(ctx)
674: 				if err != nil {
675: 					log.Errorf("could not remove container %q: %v", n.Config().LongName, err)
676: 				}
677: 			case <-ctx.Done():
678: 				return
679: 			}
680: 		}
681: 	}
682: 
683: 	// start concurrent workers
684: 	wg.Add(int(workers))
685: 
686: 	for i := range workers {
687: 		go workerFunc(i, concurrentChan, wg)
688: 	}
689: 
690: 	// send nodes to workers
691: 	for _, n := range c.Nodes {
692: 		concurrentChan <- n
693: 	}
694: 
695: 	// close channel to terminate the workers
696: 	close(concurrentChan)
697: 
698: 	// also call delete on the special nodes
699: 	specialNodes := append(
700: 		[]clablinks.Node{clablinks.GetHostLinkNode()},
701: 		clablinks.GetMgmtBrLinkNodes()...,
702: 	)
703: 	for _, n := range specialNodes {
704: 		err := n.Delete(ctx)
705: 		if err != nil {
706: 			log.Warn(err)
707: 		}
708: 	}
709: 
710: 	wg.Wait()
711: }

713: // deleteContainersDirect deletes containers directly via the runtime API.
714: // This is used when we don't have node objects (e.g., destroy-by-name-only case).
715: func (c *CLab) deleteContainersDirect(
716: 	ctx context.Context,
717: 	containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,
718: ) {
719: 	for _, cont := range containers {
720: 		if len(cont.Names) == 0 {
721: 			log.Warnf("skipping container %s with no names", cont.ID)
722: 			continue
723: 		}
724: 		name := cont.Names[0]
725: 		log.Infof("Removing container: %s", name)
726: 
727: 		c.logoutTailscaleContainer(ctx, cont)
728: 		rt := cont.Runtime
729: 		if rt == nil {
730: 			rt = c.globalRuntime()
731: 		}
732: 		err := rt.DeleteContainer(ctx, name)
733: 		if err != nil {
734: 			log.Errorf("could not remove container %q: %v", name, err)
735: 		}
736: 	}
737: }

Reasoning
Clabernetes: `clabernetesBriefLink` rejects mgmt-net links whose Network is non-default. `defaultMgmtNetwork(config.Mgmt)`: falls back to "clab" when unset. So a topology with `mgmt.network: "clab"` and a link with `network: clab` → accepted (mapped to brief, which attaches to default). A topology with `mgmt.network: custom` and link `network: custom` → REJECTED (raw.Network "custom" != mgmtNetwork "custom"? no — it equals, so accepted!). Wait: `raw.Network != "" && raw.Network != mgmtNetwork` → for mgmt.network: custom and link network: custom → accepted → brief loses the network field, attaches to default = "custom". That's actually CORRECT for clabernetes (single network = the default). And a topology with two networks (mgmt.networks: custom1, custom2, first=custom1) and link network: custom1 → `raw.Network "custom1" != mgmtNetwork "custom1"`? mgmtNetwork = mgmt.Network = "custom1" → accepted, loses network → brief attaches to default network. Default in clabernetes = config.Mgmt = custom1. Correct. Link network: custom2 → rejected with clear error. Correct behavior.

One nit: `defaultMgmtNetworkName = "clab"` — magic default. Where does containerlab get the default network name? Probably `types.MgmtNet` default — is there a constant in the codebase to reuse instead of hardcoding "clab"? Check constants. If there's an existing exported default, reusing would follow ponytail "reuse". Let me grep for default mgmt network name in types.

Now let me look at the remaining diff hunks: ownership.go (1657-1748), docker.go (1748-1791), podman.go (1791-1833), runtime.go (1833-1856), schema (1856-1873), exec.go (448-480), config.go (177-200), clab.go (111-177), apply.go (3-24), apply_test.go (24-111), network_test.go (630-953), destroy_test.go (310-448), links tests (1314-1403, 1620-1657), docs (1061-1140).

Important: `ownershipName` — for mgmtBridgeLinkNode returns "mgmt-net" instead of bridge shortname. This keeps the ownership marker STABLE across network changes. And ownership matching — `ownershipAltName` used for interface ownership; the live marker check compares live ownership vs desired? If a mgmt-net link moves networks, the live interface's ownership marker remains "mgmt-net" — so apply detects via bridgeMasterMismatch. Good design.

But — is there a compatibility concern: existing deployed labs (built by the OLD binary) have interfaces whose ownership marker recorded the BRIDGE name (since old ownershipAltName used node.GetShortName() = bridge). With the new binary, ownershipAltName uses "mgmt-net". Does apply compare live ownership marker vs desired marker? If yes, existing labs' interfaces would mismatch on apply → treated as... let me check how the ownership marker is used. Let me read ownership.go diff and its usage.

Reasoning
The `isOwnedBy` handles backward compatibility: interfaces deployed by earlier releases carry markers for the bridge name; accepted. Good — well-thought-out.

One note: `isOwnedBy(link, node, ownerName, ifaceName)` — the legacy fallback only applies to `mgmtBridgeLinkNode` AND `ownerName == mgmtNetOwnerName`. For `DiscoverOwnedInterfacesFor(ctx, node, ownerName, name)` — when ownerName != ownershipName(node)? e.g., parking nodes call with a different owner — the legacy fallback would NOT apply since node is not mgmtBridgeLinkNode. Correct.

But subtle: `DiscoverOwnedInterfacesFor` is called with `ownerName` computed by caller; in ownership.go DiscoverOwnedInterfaces passes `ownershipName(node)`. For mgmtBridgeLinkNode with resolved bridge: ownerName = "mgmt-net"; legacy acceptance for bridge name. BUT — what about interfaces deployed by earlier releases where the node shortname was... old behavior: `DiscoverOwnedInterfacesFor(ctx, node, node.GetShortName())` where the node's shortname WAS the bridge (SetMgmtNetUnderlyingBridge sets shortname). So the live marker has the bridge name. New code: primary check "mgmt-net" fails → legacy fallback checks `node.GetShortName()` = bridge → matches. Good.

Now `IsOwnedBy` — hmm, actually in the diff: `!isOwnedBy(link, node, ownerName, name)` in DiscoverOwnedInterfacesFor. Where does `node` come from in that scope? It's the function parameter `node Node`. Fine.

Wait, one more subtlety in `isOwnedBy`: legacy check `HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, node.GetShortName(), ifaceName)` — for the mgmt bridge node of a network whose shortname is "mgmt-net" (unresolved): `HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, "mgmt-net", ifaceName)` — same as primary. Fine.

Now, potential legacy issue: two mgmt-net links on DIFFERENT networks deployed by the same old binary? Old binary only had one network — fine.

Next: docker.go and podman.go diff hunks (1748-1856), schema (1856-1873), exec.go (448-480), config.go (177-200), clab.go (111-177), docs (1061-1140). Let me batch-read.

1064:  The following also should be taken into consideration:
1065:  
1066:  - Nodes using `network-mode` ignore the `mgmt-net` key.
1067:  - The `--network`, `--ipv4/6-subnet` flag is not supported.
1068:  - [`skip-when-unused`](#skipping-the-management-network) is evaluated per network: a network with the flag set is not created when every node attached to it runs with `network-mode: none`.
1069: +- [`mgmt-net` links](#additional-connections-to-management-network) attach to the first management network unless the extended link definition selects another one with the `network` key.
1070:  - When a management network is dropped from the `mgmt` list, the next `destroy` removes it together with the networks the topology still defines.
1071:  
1072:  ### Drivers
1073:  
1074:  The driver specifies the type of network that is created. Either `bridge` or `macvlan`. 
1075: @@ -727,10 +728,37 @@ topology:
1076:  
1077:  In the above example the node `n1` connects with its `e1-1` interface to the management network. This is done by specifying the endpoint with a reserved name `mgmt-net` and defining the name of the interface that should be used in that bridge (`n1-e1-1`).
1078:  
1079:  By specifying `mgmt-net` name of the node in the endpoint definition we tell containerlab to find out which bridge is used by the management network of our lab and use this bridge as the attachment point for our veth pair.
1080:  
1081: +With [multiple management networks](#multiple-management-networks) the brief form attaches to the first network in the `mgmt` list. To attach to a different network, use the [extended `mgmt-net` link](topo-def-file.md#mgmt-net) definition and set the `network` key to the name of the management network:
1082: +
1083: +```yaml
1084: +name: multi
1085: +mgmt:
1086: +  - network: oob
1087: +    ipv4-subnet: 172.31.10.0/24
1088: +  - network: lab
1089: +    ipv4-subnet: 172.31.20.0/24
1090: +    bridge: br-lab
1091: +topology:
1092: +  nodes:
1093: +    r1:
1094: +      kind: linux
1095: +      image: alpine
1096: +      mgmt-net: oob
1097: +  links:
1098: +    - type: mgmt-net
1099: +      network: lab
1100: +      endpoint:
1101: +        node: r1
1102: +        interface: eth1
1103: +      host-interface: r1-eth1
1104: +```
1105: +
1106: +The referenced network must be defined in the `mgmt` list and use the `bridge` driver.
1107: +

display:block;\" data-mxgraph=\"{&quot;page&quot;:14,&quot;zoom&quot;:1.5,&quot;highlight&quot;:&quot;#0000ff&quot;,&quot;nav&quot;:true,&quot;check-visible-state&quot;:true,&quot;resize&quot;:true,&quot;url&quot;:&quot;https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srl-labs/containerlab/diagrams/containerlab.drawio&quot;}\"></div>\n \n ### MACVLAN links\ndiff --git a/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md b/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\nindex 78ed408..11d44b5 100644\n--- a/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\n+++ b/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\n@@ -311,17 +311,20 @@ The mgmt-net link type represents a veth pair that is connected to a container n\n     endpoint:\n       node: <NodeA-Name>                    # mandatory\n       interface: <NodeA-Interface-Name>     # mandatory\n       mac: <NodeA-Interface-Mac>            # optional\n     host-interface: <interface-name>        # mandatory\n+    network: <mgmt-network-name>            # optional\n     mtu: <link-mtu>                         # optional\n     vars: <link-variables>                  # optional (used in templating)\n     labels: <link-labels>                   # optional (used in templating)\n ```\n \n The `host-interface` is the desired interface name that will be attached to the management network in the host namespace.\n \n+The `network` selects one of the [multiple management networks](network.md#multiple-management-networks) by its name. When omitted, the link attaches to the first management network. The selected network must use the `bridge` driver.\n+\n ###### macvlan\n \n The macvlan link type creates a MACVlan interface with the `host-interface` as its parent interface. The MACVlan interface is then moved to a node's network namespace and renamed to the `endpoint.interface` name.\n \n ```yaml\ndiff --git a/labruntime/clabernetes/files.go b/labruntime/clabernetes/files.go\nindex d1331cf..c017714 100644\n--- a/labruntime/clabernetes/files.go\n+++ b/labruntime/clabernetes/files.go\n@@ -39,10 +39,14 @@ const (\n \n \tclabDirVar     = \"__clabDir__\"\n \tclabLabNameVar = \"__clabLabName__\"\n \tnodeDirVar     = \"__clabNodeDir__\"\n \tnodeNameVar    = \"__clabNodeName__\"\n+\n+\t// defaultMgmtNetworkName is the management network name containerlab uses when\n+\t// the topology does not set one.\n+\tdefaultMgmtNetworkName = \"clab\"\n )\n \n var (\n \tinvalidDNSLabelChars = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-z0-9\\-]`) //nolint:gochecknoglobals\n \tstartsWithNonAlpha   = regexp.MustCompile(`^[^a-z]`)     //nolint:gochecknoglobals\n@@ -244,11 +248,14 @@ func renderClabernetesTopologyDefinition(\n \t\tMgmt:     config.Mgmt,\n \t\tSettings: config.Settings,\n \t}\n \n \tif config.Topology != nil {\n-\t\tlinks, err := clabernetesBriefLinks(config.Topology.Links)\n+\t\tlinks, err := clabernetesBriefLinks(\n+\t\t\tconfig.Topology.Links,\n+\t\t\tdefaultMgmtNetwork(config.Mgmt),\n+\t\t)\n \t\tif err != nil {\n \t\t\treturn nil, err\n \t\t}\n \t\trenameBriefLinkEndpoints(links, renames)\n \n@@ -264,10 +271,11 @@ func renderClabernetesTopologyDefinition(\n \treturn yaml.Marshal(rendered)\n }\n \n func clabernetesBriefLinks(\n \tlinks []*clablinks.LinkDefinition,\n+\tmgmtNetwork string,\n ) ([]*clablinks.LinkBriefRaw, error) {\n \tif len(links) == 0 {\n \t\treturn nil, nil\n \t}\n \n@@ -275,11 +283,11 @@ func clabernetesBriefLinks(\n \tfor _, link := range links {\n \t\tif link == nil || link.Link == nil {\n \t\t\tcontinue\n \t\t}\n ",

379: func setMgmtNetworkDefaults(m *clabtypes.MgmtNet, isDefault bool) error {
380: 	if m.Network == "" {
381: 		m.Network = dockerNetName
382: 	}
383: 
384: 	// extra networks without subnets get them from the runtime's address pools,
385: 	// node addresses within them are still assigned by the IPAM provider
386: 	if isDefault && m.Driver != clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {
387: 		if m.IPv4Subnet == "" && m.IPv6Subnet == "" {
388: 			// assign the default subnets

390: 			m.IPv6Subnet = dockerNetIPv6Addr
391: 		}
392: 	}
393: 
394: 	// by default external access is enabled if not set by a user

401: 		m.IPAM.Provider = clabtypes.IPAMProviderContainerlab
402: 	}
403:

405: }

407: // mgmtNetByName returns the management network a node selected with mgmt-net.
408: // An empty name selects the default network.
409: func (c *CLab) mgmtNetByName(network string) (*clabtypes.MgmtNet, error) {
410: 	if network == "" {
411: 		return c.Config.Mgmt, nil
412: 	}
413: 	for _, m := range c.Config.MgmtNetworks {
414: 		if m.Network == network {
415: 			return m, nil
416: 		}
417: 	}
418: 	return nil, fmt.Errorf("management network %q is not defined in the mgmt section", network)
419: }

So unresolved → setMgmtNetLinkBridges sets shortname "" → verify fails.

Hmm — but hold on, wait. Would the network exist in this scenario? apply on existing lab: user adds a NEW network to the mgmt list (say `lab` with ipv4-subnet) plus a mgmt-net link with network: lab. The network doesn't exist in the runtime. resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks → not found → unresolved. Verify fails with `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`.

But actually — wait, is `c.Config.Mgmt.Bridge` (the default) resolved? Yes (setMgmtBridgeFromRuntime from container labels). So only the new network fails.

Now, another potential issue: **`ownershipAltName` for the mgmt bridge endpoint used when CREATING interfaces** (link.go:680: `altName := ownershipAltName(endpt)`). New deployments create markers "mgmt-net". Legacy labs' interfaces have bridge markers. On apply, validation accepts legacy. On new interface creation, "mgmt-net". OK.

Reasoning
`tools veth` uses plain bridge endpoints (`bridge:` / `ovs-bridge:` first block), not mgmt-net. So removing `SetMgmtNetUnderlyingBridge` from exec is safe. Good.

Now let me check `save.go` — removed the call too. Save only copies files. Safe.

Now check network_test.go hunks (630-953) for coverage of the new behavior, and links tests (1314-1403, 1620-1657). Then check remaining docs hunks are already seen. Then finalize.

Also — one more issue candidate to verify: in `setMgmtNetLinkBridges`, networks whose bridge is "" (unresolved/missing) get shortname "". When `resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` SKIPPED a network because mgmtRuntime errored (podman), the network's mgmt-net link resolves with shortname "mgmt-net"... wait no — setMgmtNetLinkBridges unconditionally calls `SetMgmtNetworkUnderlyingBridge(m.Network, m.Bridge)` → sets shortname "" (since m.Bridge == ""). Then verify → CheckBridgeExists("") fails cryptically. For podman + apply with non-default network defined in topology (network doesn't exist, podman can't create) → cryptic `bridge ""` error instead of the clearer "runtime does not support multiple management networks". Hmm — that's the same root cause as F1 (empty shortname not tolerated / surfaced). One finding covers both: the empty-bridge shortname surfaces as `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist` in apply verification.

Now the test coverage check: network_test.go — let me scan the new tests quickly.

Wait — I notice something in the tests: the tests use `mgmt` list entries WITH explicit `bridge: br-sel-oob` / `br-sel-lab` — so `m.Bridge` is set from the topology. But the docs example uses `bridge: br-lab` too. What about a network WITHOUT an explicit bridge — the bridge comes from the runtime (docker auto `br-<id>`). resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks handles that. OK.

Note: test `TestMgmtNetLinkSelectsNetwork` — the first mgmt network IS the default (r1's mgmt-net selects "mgmtnet-select-oob"). And the mgmt-net link without `network` key attaches to the first network (default) — want r1-eth1 → br-sel-oob. Consistent with resolve mapping network == DefaultMgmtNetwork → "" → default node. Good.

Let me read the rest of network_test.go hunks (790-953) — the remaining tests for skipMgmtNetwork and podman error.
