1062: +++ b/docs/manual/network.md
1063: @@ -274,10 +274,11 @@ The first defined management network becomes the default network for things like
1064:  The following also should be taken into consideration:
1065:  
1066:  - Nodes using `network-mode` ignore the `mgmt-net` key.
1067:  - The `--network`, `--ipv4/6-subnet` flag is not supported.
1068:  - [`skip-when-unused`](#skipping-the-management-network) is evaluated per network: a network with the flag set is not created when every node attached to it runs with `network-mode: none`.
1069: +- [`mgmt-net` links](#additional-connections-to-management-network) attach to the first management network unless the extended link definition selects another one with the `network` key.
1070:  - When a management network is dropped from the `mgmt` list, the next `destroy` removes it together with the networks the topology still defines.
1071:  
1072:  ### Drivers
1073:  
1074:  The driver specifies the type of network that is created. Either `bridge` or `macvlan`. 
1075: @@ -727,10 +728,37 @@ topology:
1076:  
1077:  In the above example the node `n1` connects with its `e1-1` interface to the management network. This is done by specifying the endpoint with a reserved name `mgmt-net` and defining the name of the interface that should be used in that bridge (`n1-e1-1`).
1078:  
1079:  By specifying `mgmt-net` name of the node in the endpoint definition we tell containerlab to find out which bridge is used by the management network of our lab and use this bridge as the attachment point for our veth pair.
1080:  
1081: +With [multiple management networks](#multiple-management-networks) the brief form attaches to the first network in the `mgmt` list. To attach to a different network, use the [extended `mgmt-net` link](topo-def-file.md#mgmt-net) definition and set the `network` key to the name of the management network:
1082: +
1083: +```yaml
1084: +name: multi
1085: +mgmt:
1086: +  - network: oob
1087: +    ipv4-subnet: 172.31.10.0/24
1088: +  - network: lab
1089: +    ipv4-subnet: 172.31.20.0/24
1090: +    bridge: br-lab
1091: +topology:
1092: +  nodes:
1093: +    r1:
1094: +      kind: linux
1095: +      image: alpine
1096: +      mgmt-net: oob
1097: +  links:
1098: +    - type: mgmt-net
1099: +      network: lab
1100: +      endpoint:
1101: +        node: r1
1102: +        interface: eth1
1103: +      host-interface: r1-eth1
1104: +```
1105: +
1106: +The referenced network must be defined in the `mgmt` list and use the `bridge` driver.
1107: +
1108:  This is best illustrated with the following diagram:
1109:  
1110:  <div class="mxgraph" style="max-width:100%;border:1px solid transparent;margin:0 auto; display:block;" data-mxgraph="{&quot;page&quot;:14,&quot;zoom&quot;:1.5,&quot;highlight&quot;:&quot;#0000ff&quot;,&quot;nav&quot;:true,&quot;check-visible-state&quot;:true,&quot;resize&quot;:true,&quot;url&quot;:&quot;https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srl-labs/containerlab/diagrams/containerlab.drawio&quot;}"></div>

Reasoning
Interesting! The Podman diff adds `ResolveMgmtBridge` with a `var _ runtime.MgmtBridgeResolver = (*PodmanRuntime)(nil)` assertion. But earlier I found `MgmtNetBinder.ForMgmtNet` is only implemented by Docker — so Podman satisfies `MgmtBridgeResolver` but not `MgmtNetBinder`. Then `mgmtRuntime` still errors for Podman when non-default networks are referenced by mgmt-net links. OK — F2 stands but the podman resolver exists for... the DEFAULT network? `resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` iterates mgmtNetLinkNetworks() — if the podman topology has NO mgmt-net links with explicit network, mgmtNetLinkNetworks returns empty? Let me check `mgmtNetLinkNetworks()` — iterates mgmt-net links; for links without network or with the default network → adds default (maybe only when >=1 non-default or any?). Let me verify: if there are only default-attaching mgmt-net links, does mgmtNetLinkNetworks include the default network? From my earlier read: "networks referenced by mgmt-net links... default network added when referenced (possibly skipped for DefaultMgmtNetwork)". The podman resolver would then be used for the default network when mgmt-net links exist. That makes sense: apply with podman + a default mgmt-net link → resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks resolves the default bridge via podman. And non-default networks error via mgmtRuntime. Consistent.

Wait — one more check on `ResolveMgmtBridge` in podman: `if err != nil || !exists { return err }` — fine.

Docker's ResolveMgmtBridge: fine.

Now — the schema hunk: adds `network` to mgmt-net link properties. Good — schema updated.

Now let me double check the one remaining verification piece for F1: confirm that `CheckBridgeExists` is actually invoked during apply verification for the empty-shortname endpoint, i.e. `EndpointBridge.Verify`. Let me read endpoint_bridge.go quickly to be sure of the exact behavior and error text.

However, the error for podman on apply is cryptic (`bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`) because Podman implements `MgmtBridgeResolver`, so `resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` proceeds (does not error) and sets an empty bridge; `mgmtRuntime` errors only for `MgmtNetBinder`... wait let me re-check: `mgmtRuntime` returns error when `!hasMgmtNetBinder && m.Network != DefaultMgmtNetwork`. For Podman: no ForMgmtNet → error `runtime %q does not support multiple management networks`. That error is raised in `resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` for non-default networks... but only when the network is referenced by a mgmt-net link? Let me re-read resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks: it iterates mgmtNetLinkNetworks() — networks referenced by mgmt-net links (including default when referenced). For each non-default network: mgmtRuntime(m) → error for podman. So the podman path: apply with mgmt-net link to non-default network → clean error `runtime "podman" does not support multiple management networks`. Good — that's clean, not cryptic. F2 downgrades: the podman limitation is documented and the error is clean. Drop F2 as a finding, or keep as P4? Actually wait — what about podman with a topology having a mgmt-net link to the default network only? resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks: networks referenced = default (added when referenced). For default: `hasMgmtNetBinder || m.Network == DefaultMgmtNetwork` → skip (no error). Then ResolveMgmtBridge (podman implements) resolves default bridge. Then setMgmtNetLinkBridges. Works. Good — podman works for default-network mgmt-net links.

Reasoning
Very important detail in `resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` (network.go:188-193): `mgmtRuntime` errors are LOGGED and SKIPPED, not returned! So for Podman with a non-default mgmt-net link: `mgmtRuntime` error is swallowed (log.Debug) → no resolver resolution → `m.Bridge` stays "" → `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` sets shortname "" → verify → `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`. So the podman error path IS cryptic after all — the "runtime does not support multiple management networks" error is only surfaced in the fresh-deploy path (`createNetworks` → `mgmtRuntime` → returns error), but in apply it's swallowed and manifests as the cryptic empty-bridge error. And for Podman the docs say multiple mgmt networks are Docker-only; the error surfaced to the user on apply is `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist` — confusing but arguably acceptable given documented Docker-only support. This strengthens F1: the root cause is the unresolved (empty) bridge shortname surfacing cryptically in apply verification. One finding covers both podman-swallowed-error and missing-network cases.

Note also: the missing-network case on apply — the comment on `TestResolveMgmtNetLinkNetworksAutoBridge` "missing network is not created" indicates the empty-bridge state is intended to be tolerated (like bridgeMasterMismatch's skip). So the correction: make `EndpointBridge.Verify` (or `CheckBridgeExists`) tolerate an empty shortname for mgmt-net (nodeless) endpoints, or skip verification for unresolved mgmt-net bridges in verifyLinks. Also the empty-name node is passed to other code paths (deployLink via LinkByName("") would fail with a similar error if deploy actually proceeded — but verify failing first prevents that).

Also note `mgmtRuntime` error is swallowed only in resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks; in createNetworks it returns the error (fresh deploy). For consistency the apply path could surface the podman error rather than the cryptic empty-bridge failure. But minimal correction: tolerate unresolved bridge in verification (consistent with bridgeMasterMismatch) — the empty bridge then fails later at deployLinks with `LinkByName("")`... hmm, wait. If verify tolerates it, deploy proceeds: linkNeedsDeploy → added → deployLinks → EndpointBridge.Deploy → LinkByName("") → fails with "Link not found" or similar. Still cryptic but at deploy time... Hmm.

Actually think about the correct minimal behavior for apply adding a NEW network + mgmt-net link: after verify, `prepareApply` runs `createNetworks` → creates the new network → docker CreateNet sets m.Bridge. But wait — `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` was already called BEFORE prepareApply (apply.go:137). The node shortname remains "" during deployLinks. So even tolerating the empty bridge in verify, deployLinks would try LinkByName("") and fail. UNLESS deployLinks re-resolves... Let me check: does the deploy of a mgmt-net link re-read the node's shortname? The endpoint's node IS the mgmtBridgeLinkNode — shortname "" until setMgmtNetLinkBridges runs again. After prepareApply creates the network, deploy.go:320 calls `setMgmtNetLinkBridges()` again (per my earlier trace: prepareLabManagementNetwork → CreateNetwork → setMgmtNetLinkBridges at deploy.go:320). So by deployLinks time (after prepareApply), shortname = actual bridge → deploy succeeds. So the ONLY blocker is verify failing on empty bridge before network creation. Tolerating empty bridge in verification for nodeless mgmt-net endpoints makes the whole flow work. That's the minimal correction, consistent with bridgeMasterMismatch's existing tolerance and the test's documented intent.

Let me double check deploy.go:320 to confirm setMgmtNetLinkBridges runs after network creation in prepareApply.

# Code Review: mgmt-net links for multiple management networks

## Summary

This PR extends `mgmt-net` links so they can attach to any management network defined in the `mgmt` list (not only the first/default one), introduces per-network `mgmtBridgeLinkNode`s, a stable `mgmt-net` ownership marker (with backward compatibility for interfaces deployed by earlier releases that carry the bridge-name marker), a runtime `MgmtBridgeResolver` capability, reconciler tolerance for moved/missing bridges, clabernetes brief-link rejection of non-default networks, docs, and schema support.

The overall design is sound: the `bridgeMasterMismatch` tolerance, legacy ownership-marker fallback, and destroy-path network resolution are all well-reasoned, and the added tests cover the main flows. I traced the fresh-deploy, apply, plan, and destroy paths end to end and found one real functional gap in the apply path, plus two optional polish items.

| Priority | Title |
|---|---|
| P2 | `apply` cannot add a `mgmt-net` link on a management network that does not exist yet; verification fails with a cryptic `bridge ""` error |
| P4 | Magic string `"mgmt-net"` duplicated in `bridgeMasterMismatch` instead of reusing `mgmtNetOwnerName` |
| P4 | `defaultMgmtNetworkName = "clab"` duplicates `dockerNetName` |

---

## Findings

### P2 — `apply` cannot add a `mgmt-net` link on a management network that does not exist yet; verification fails with a cryptic `bridge ""` error

**Location:** [core/apply.go L130-L148](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/apply.go#L130-L148), with the mechanism in [links/endpoint_bridge.go L62-L71](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/links/endpoint_bridge.go#L62-L71) and the state producer in [core/network.go L207-L220](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/network.go#L207-L220).

**Problem:** When a management network referenced by a `mgmt-net` link does not exist (or cannot be resolved by the runtime), `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` deliberately leaves the link node's shortname empty (`SetMgmtNetworkUnderlyingBridge(m.Network, m.Bridge)` with `m.Bridge == ""`). The PR acknowledges this state is expected: `bridgeMasterMismatch` (core/topology_reconcile.go:928-943) skips nodeless endpoints with an empty bridge, and `TestResolveMgmtNetLinkNetworksAutoBridge` explicitly asserts `wantBridge: ""` for a "missing network is not created" case. However, the apply path runs `checkApplyTopologyDefinition` (apply.go:146) — which calls `Link.Verify` with `RunBridgeExistsCheck: true` — **before** `prepareApply` (apply.go:198) creates the missing networks. `CheckBridgeExists` calls `netlink.LinkByName(n.GetShortName())` and reports `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`.

**Trigger:** A user edits a deployed topology to add a new entry to the `mgmt` list plus a `mgmt-net` link with `network: <new-network>` (bridge driver, no explicit bridge), then runs `clab apply` (or `clab deploy` reconcile on an existing lab). Also reachable on Podman: `resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` swallows the `mgmtRuntime` error at core/network.go:188-193 (`log.Debug` and continue), so even the otherwise-clear "runtime does not support multiple management networks" message never surfaces on apply; the user instead sees the empty-bridge error.

**Impact:** The headline scenario for the feature — incrementally adding a management network and attaching links to it via apply — fails before apply ever gets a chance to create the network. Fresh deploy works only because deploy creates networks (`prepareLabManagementNetwork`, core/deploy.go:306-321) before `checkTopologyDefinition` and re-runs `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` after `CreateNetwork`. The error message (`bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`) gives the user no actionable guidance.

**Correction:** Tolerate an unresolved bridge in verification the same way `bridgeMasterMismatch` already does — e.g. in `EndpointBridge.Verify`/`CheckBridgeExists`, skip the bridge-existence check when the node is a nodeless mgmt-net endpoint with an empty shortname (or return the resolution duty to a single place by exporting that check from the links package). With that tolerance, the existing apply flow completes correctly: `prepareApply` → `CreateNetwork` sets `m.Bridge` → `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` re-points the node → `deployLinks` deploys against the real bridge. If the intended design is instead "apply may only attach to existing networks", then surface a clear error at `setMgmtNetLinkBridges`/`resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` time (including the swallowed `mgmtRuntime` error) rather than letting the empty shortname reach verification.

### P4 — Magic string `"mgmt-net"` duplicated in `bridgeMasterMismatch` instead of reusing `mgmtNetOwnerName`

**Location:** [core/topology_reconcile.go L928-L943](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/topology_reconcile.go#L928-L943) versus [links/link_mgmt-net.go L115-L119](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/links/link_mgmt-net.go#L115-L119).

**Problem:** The new `bridgeMasterMismatch` helper hardcodes the nodeless skip condition `bridge == "mgmt-net"`, duplicating the owner name that the links package already centralizes as `mgmtNetOwnerName`. The constant is unexported, so `core` cannot reference it directly today.

**Trigger:** Any future change to the logical owner name (or a rename of the special node name) silently breaks the reconciler's skip condition while the links package keeps working.

**Impact:** Low; a maintenance consistency issue only. The two spellings are semantically the same logical name by design of this PR.

**Correction (optional):** Either export the constant from the `links` package (it is already part of the package's public-ish vocabulary, e.g. `GetMgmtBrLinkNodes`) and use it in `bridgeMasterMismatch`, or move the skip predicate into the `links` package so `core` does not need to know the marker scheme.

### P4 — `defaultMgmtNetworkName = "clab"` duplicates `dockerNetName`

**Location:** [labruntime/clabernetes/files.go L44-L47](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/labruntime/clabernetes/files.go#L44-L47) versus [core/config.go L33](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/config.go#L33).

**Problem:** The new clabernetes constant `defaultMgmtNetworkName = "clab"` restates the default management network name that `core/config.go` already owns as `dockerNetName`.

**Trigger:** Any change to the default network name in `core` leaves the clabernetes fallback silently out of sync, producing brief links that attach to a network name that never matches `defaultMgmtNetwork(config.Mgmt)` in one of the two packages.

**Impact:** Low; both values are `"clab"` today and the duplication is confined to one fallback expression.

**Correction (optional):** Export the constant from `core` (e.g. `DefaultMgmtNetName`) and use it in `labruntime/clabernetes`, or have the clabernetes default flow through the same code path that resolves `config.Mgmt` defaults.

---

## Coverage Notes

- This was a source-only review of the head revision (`1afdbb9`); no tests were executed and no code was run.
- Traced end to end: fresh deploy ordering (`ResolveLinks` before `prepareLabManagementNetwork`, so unresolved bridges never reach verification on a clean deploy — confirmed correct), the apply ordering (`apply.go:130-198`, source of the P2 finding), `planApply` endpoint discovery for the logical `mgmt-net` node across networks (all networks' link nodes live in the root namespace, so the single `"mgmt-net"` discovery key is sound), ownership marker creation (`ownershipAltName` now uses the stable owner), legacy compatibility (`isOwnedBy` accepts bridge-name markers from earlier releases, covered by `TestIsOwnedByMgmtNetNode`), destroy (`WithSkippedMgmtNetLinksCheck`, `resolveExistingMgmtNetworks` never creates networks, `GetMgmtBrLinkNodes` in special-node deletion), clabernetes brief-link rejection (correct: the brief form has no `network` field, so non-default networks must be refused), and the schema addition for the `network` key.
- The Podman limitation (no `MgmtNetBinder`/`ForMgmtNet`) is intentional and documented in `docs/rn/0.80.md:72` ("Multiple management networks are currently supported with the Docker runtime only"); Podman still implements `MgmtBridgeResolver` for default-network `mgmt-net` links. The cryptic error Podman users see on apply is captured as part of the P2 finding rather than a separate defect.
- The package-level `_mgmtBrLinkNodes` map is shared across labs in one process (pre-existing pattern, previously a single node). Keys are network names, which bounds the cross-lab interaction to same-named networks; no defect found, noted for awareness.
- `exec.go` and `save.go` removals of `SetMgmtNetUnderlyingBridge` are safe: those flows do not resolve or deploy mgmt-net links, and `tools veth` uses plain bridge endpoints.
- Documentation updates in `docs/manual/network.md` and `docs/manual/topo-def-file.md` accurately describe the new `network` key, the default-network fallback, and the bridge-driver requirement.

# Code Review: mgmt-net links for multiple management networks

## Summary

This PR extends `mgmt-net` links so they can attach to any management network defined in the `mgmt` list (not only the first/default one). It introduces per-network `mgmtBridgeLinkNode`s, a stable `mgmt-net` ownership marker (with backward compatibility for interfaces deployed by earlier releases that carry the bridge-name marker), a runtime `MgmtBridgeResolver` capability, reconciler tolerance for moved/unresolved bridges, clabernetes brief-link rejection of non-default networks, plus docs and schema support.

The design is sound: the `bridgeMasterMismatch` tolerance, the legacy ownership-marker fallback, and the destroy-path network resolution are all well-reasoned, and the added tests cover the main flows. I traced the fresh-deploy, apply, plan, and destroy paths end to end and found one real functional gap in the apply path, plus two optional polish items.

| Priority | Title |
|---|---|
| P2 | `apply` cannot add a `mgmt-net` link on a management network that does not exist yet; verification fails with a cryptic `bridge ""` error |
| P4 | Magic string `"mgmt-net"` duplicated in `bridgeMasterMismatch` instead of reusing `mgmtNetOwnerName` |
| P4 | `defaultMgmtNetworkName = "clab"` duplicates `dockerNetName` |

---

## Findings

### P2 — `apply` cannot add a `mgmt-net` link on a management network that does not exist yet; verification fails with a cryptic `bridge ""` error

**Location:** [core/apply.go L130-L148](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/apply.go#L130-L148), with the mechanism in [links/endpoint_bridge.go L62-L71](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/links/endpoint_bridge.go#L62-L71) and the state producer in [core/network.go L207-L220](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/network.go#L207-L220).

**Problem:** When a management network referenced by a `mgmt-net` link does not exist (or cannot be resolved by the runtime), `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` deliberately leaves the link node's shortname empty (`SetMgmtNetworkUnderlyingBridge(m.Network, m.Bridge)` with `m.Bridge == ""`). The PR acknowledges this state as expected: `bridgeMasterMismatch` (core/topology_reconcile.go:928-943) skips nodeless endpoints with an empty bridge, and `TestResolveMgmtNetLinkNetworksAutoBridge` explicitly asserts `wantBridge: ""` for its "missing network is not created" case. However, the apply path runs `checkApplyTopologyDefinition` (apply.go:146) — which calls `Link.Verify` with `RunBridgeExistsCheck: true` — **before** `prepareApply` (apply.go:198) creates the missing networks. `CheckBridgeExists` calls `netlink.LinkByName(n.GetShortName())` and reports `bridge "" referenced in topology but does not exist`.

**Trigger:** A user edits a deployed topology to add a new entry to the `mgmt` list plus a `mgmt-net` link with `network: <new-network>` (bridge driver, no explicit bridge), then runs `clab apply` (or a reconcile `clab deploy` on the existing lab). The same path is reachable on Podman: `resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` swallows the `mgmtRuntime` error at core/network.go:188-193 (`log.Debug` and continue), so the otherwise-clear "runtime does not support multiple management networks" message never surfaces on apply; the user instead sees the empty-bridge error.

**Impact:** The headline scenario for the feature — incrementally adding a management network and attaching links to it via apply — fails before apply ever gets a chance to create the network. Fresh deploy works only because deploy creates networks (`prepareLabManagementNetwork`, core/deploy.go:306-321) before `checkTopologyDefinition` and re-runs `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` after `CreateNetwork`. The error message gives the user no actionable guidance.

**Correction:** Tolerate an unresolved bridge in verification the same way `bridgeMasterMismatch` already does — for example, skip the bridge-existence check in `EndpointBridge.Verify`/`CheckBridgeExists` when the node is a nodeless mgmt-net endpoint with an empty shortname (or centralize that tolerance in the links package). With that tolerance, the existing apply flow completes correctly: `prepareApply` → `CreateNetwork` sets `m.Bridge` → `setMgmtNetLinkBridges` re-points the node → `deployLinks` deploys against the real bridge. If the intended design is instead "apply may only attach to existing networks", then surface a clear error at `setMgmtNetLinkBridges`/`resolveMgmtNetLinkNetworks` time (including the currently swallowed `mgmtRuntime` error) rather than letting the empty shortname reach verification.

### P4 — Magic string `"mgmt-net"` duplicated in `bridgeMasterMismatch` instead of reusing `mgmtNetOwnerName`

**Location:** [core/topology_reconcile.go L928-L943](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/topology_reconcile.go#L928-L943) versus [links/link_mgmt-net.go L115-L119](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/links/link_mgmt-net.go#L115-L119).

**Problem:** The new `bridgeMasterMismatch` helper hardcodes the nodeless skip condition `bridge == "mgmt-net"`, duplicating the owner name that the links package already centralizes as `mgmtNetOwnerName`. The constant is unexported, so `core` cannot reference it directly today.

**Trigger:** Any future change to the logical owner name (or a rename of the special node name) silently breaks the reconciler's skip condition while the links package keeps working.

**Impact:** Low; a maintenance consistency issue only. The two spellings are semantically the same logical name by this PR's design.

**Correction (optional):** Either export the constant from the `links` package (it is already part of the package's public vocabulary, e.g. `GetMgmtBrLinkNodes`) and use it in `bridgeMasterMismatch`, or move the skip predicate into the `links` package so `core` does not need to know the marker scheme.

### P4 — `defaultMgmtNetworkName = "clab"` duplicates `dockerNetName`

**Location:** [labruntime/clabernetes/files.go L45-L47](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/labruntime/clabernetes/files.go#L45-L47) versus [core/config.go L33](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/1afdbb948c5267b69806c3b42f36b617ef70f34c/core/config.go#L33).

**Problem:** The new clabernetes constant `defaultMgmtNetworkName = "clab"` restates the default management network name that `core/config.go` already owns as `dockerNetName`.

**Trigger:** Any change to the default network name in `core` leaves the clabernetes fallback silently out of sync, producing brief links whose default-network matching diverges between the two packages.

**Impact:** Low; both values are `"clab"` today and the duplication is confined to one fallback expression.

**Correction (optional):** Export the constant from `core` (for example as `DefaultMgmtNetName`) and use it in `labruntime/clabernetes`, or have the clabernetes default flow through the same code path that resolves `config.Mgmt` defaults.

---

## Coverage Notes

- This was a source-only review of the head revision (`1afdbb9`); no tests were executed and no code was run.
- Traced end to end: fresh deploy ordering (`ResolveLinks` runs before `prepareLabManagementNetwork`, so unresolved bridges never reach verification on a clean deploy — confirmed correct), the apply ordering (`apply.go:130-198`, source of the P2 finding), `planApply` endpoint discovery for the logical `mgmt-net` node across networks (all networks' link nodes live in the root namespace, so the single `"mgmt-net"` discovery key is sound), ownership marker creation (`ownershipAltName` now uses the stable owner), legacy compatibility (`isOwnedBy` accepts bridge-name markers from earlier releases, covered by `TestIsOwnedByMgmtNetNode`), destroy (`WithSkippedMgmtNetLinksCheck`, `resolveExistingMgmtNetworks` never creates networks, `GetMgmtBrLinkNodes` in special-node deletion), clabernetes brief-link rejection (correct: the brief form has no `network` field, so non-default networks must be refused), and the schema addition for the `network` key.
- The Podman limitation (no `MgmtNetBinder`/`ForMgmtNet`) is intentional and documented in `docs/rn/0.80.md:72` ("Multiple management networks are currently supported with the Docker runtime only"); Podman still implements `MgmtBridgeResolver` for default-network `mgmt-net` links. The cryptic error Podman users see on apply is captured as part of the P2 finding rather than a separate defect.
- The package-level `_mgmtBrLinkNodes` map is shared across labs in one process (a pre-existing pattern, previously a single node). Keys are network names, which bounds the cross-lab interaction to same-named networks; no defect found, noted for awareness.
- The removals of `SetMgmtNetUnderlyingBridge` from `core/exec.go` and `core/save.go` are safe: those flows do not resolve or deploy mgmt-net links, and `tools veth` uses plain bridge endpoints.
- Documentation updates in `docs/manual/network.md` and `docs/manual/topo-def-file.md` accurately describe the new `network` key, the default-network fallback, and the bridge-driver requirement.
